inventory.name: gamepadrawinputchanged event on window (GamepadRawInputChangeEvent; the ChromeStatus summary's older name rawgamepadinputchange is carried as a disclosed divergence) — fires when the gamepad hardware reports a new input frame, at the device's native polling rate independent of requestAnimationFrame
event.gamepad — a snapshot Gamepad object delivered to the listener, exposing index, buttons (GamepadButton[] with pressed/touched/value), axes (values in [-1, 1]), and timestamp
GamepadRawInputChangeEvent changed-index attributes — axesChanged, buttonsValueChanged, buttonsPressed, buttonsReleased, touchesChanged (FrozenArray<long> indices of what changed in this input frame)

syntax.rationale: Coord ruling 2(b) carried forward through the 2026-10-25 upgrade: the page now has a verbatim-IDL pre block in the 'syntax and shape of the API' section, and the call form in #example is window.addEventListener('gamepadrawinputchanged', (event) => { handleInput(event.gamepad); }). The event is delivered on window; the interface is GamepadRawInputChangeEvent.

errors.rationale: The page documents no error or exception path: the #gamepad-event table lists only the event target (window), the firing condition (hardware reports new data), and the Gamepad snapshot fields, with no throwing or failure surface. The W3C Gamepad working draft (fetched 2026-10-06) does not name rawgamepadinputchange at all, and the ChromeStatus record carries no event-specific error behaviour.

securityPrivacy.rationale: The page documents no security or privacy surface: #why-it-exists motivates the event purely as a latency reduction (polling at 60 Hz vs device reports at 1000 Hz or higher), reading state that was already obtainable via navigator.getGamepads(). The ChromeStatus record (fetched 2026-10-06) has privacy_review_status and security_review_status both 'Pending' and an empty security_risks field, so no reviewed security/privacy consideration exists for the page to document.

syntax.rationale: The access form a reader writes to reach this snapshot is shown in the #example block: const { gamepad } = event; then gamepad.axes[0] and gamepad.timestamp. That is the real declaration/access grammar; the snapshot is inherited from GamepadEvent.gamepad per Chromium's gamepad_event.idl.

errors.rationale: The #gamepad-event table documents the snapshot's fields (index, buttons, axes, timestamp) as plain reads of a Gamepad object and defines no error path: reading a field of the existing Gamepad interface has no throwing surface, and the page lists no failure mode. The ChromeStatus record (fetched 2026-10-06) defines none either.

securityPrivacy.rationale: The snapshot exposes button/axis/timestamp values that the existing polling Gamepad API already returned, so the page documents no new data exposure: #why-it-exists frames the change as timing (event delivery vs polling), not as a new category of information. The ChromeStatus record (fetched 2026-10-06) carries no reviewed security/privacy consideration for the event.

errors.rationale: The five attributes are readonly FrozenArray<long> reads on a delivered event object; neither the Chromium IDL nor the explainer defines any throwing or failure surface for reading them, and the page documents none.

securityPrivacy.rationale: The changed-index arrays expose which buttons/axes changed — a strict subset of the state the polling API already returns on every getGamepads() call; the page documents no new data exposure and the ChromeStatus record carries no reviewed security/privacy consideration (re-checked 2026-10-25).
